issue_context.title: eth/fetcher fails nilness static analysis check
issue_context.body:
#### System information

Geth version: develop
OS & Version: Linux
Commit hash : 08e782c61ff5eb1f5890238c970c95bc6d19c3a6

#### Expected behaviour

```
go run golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/passes/nilness/cmd/nilness github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/eth/fetcher
# no results
```

#### Actual behaviour

```
go run golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/passes/nilness/cmd/nilness github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/eth/fetcher
-: impossible condition: non-nil == nil
exit status 3
```

#### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

```
go get -u golang.org/x/tools/...
go run golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/passes/nilness/cmd/nilness github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/eth/fetcher
```

Due to https://github.com/golang/go/issues/31008, the nilness check results returns almost no helpful information. 
I'm not sure exactly where the nilness check is failing. 
The nilness check result does not return the filename, line number, or autofix. 

More info on this analysis check
```
The nilness checker inspects the control-flow graph of each function in
a package and reports nil pointer dereferences, degenerate nil
pointers, and panics with nil values. A degenerate comparison is of the form
x==nil or x!=nil where x is statically known to be nil or non-nil. These are
often a mistake, especially in control flow related to errors. Panics with nil
values are checked because they are not detectable by
	if r := recover(); r != nil {
This check reports conditions such as:
	if f == nil { // impossible condition (f is a function)
	}
and:
	p := &v
	...
	if p != nil { // tautological condition
	}
and:
	if p == nil {
		print(*p) // nil dereference
	}
and:
	if p == nil {
		panic(p)
	}
```
